written.myAnswer: Plant cells usually have one large central vacuole that stores water and other substances and helps maintain turgor pressure. Animal cells usually have smaller vacuoles, if present.
Lysosomes contain enzymes that digest waste materials and help recycle cellular components.
Waste materials and damaged cell components may accumulate because they are not broken down and recycled properly.
The plant cell wall is a rigid layer made mainly of cellulose outside the cell membrane. It supports and protects the cell and helps it maintain its shape.
Water enters the cell and accumulates in the central vacuole, which swells and pushes the cell contents against the rigid cell wall. This pressure is called turgor pressure.

Plant cells have a cellulose cell wall, chloroplasts, and usually a large central vacuole; animal cells lack a rigid cell wall and chloroplasts and generally have smaller vacuoles. Plant cells have plasmodesmata, while animal cells have centrioles and lysosomes.
